_comment: Corrected instance-write merge task for the LCM Create action workflow. Original data_to_merge only included vnet_name and vlan_id, but schema.required lists 4 fields: subscription_id, resource_group, vnet_name, vlan_id. All 4 must be present or the post-provisioning instance write will fail and the resource will be orphaned from LCM.
_notes: This assumes subscription_id and resource_group are genuine workflow inputs supplied by the operator/form, exactly like vnet_name and vlan_id already are. If subscription_id or resource_group are instead produced by an earlier task in the workflow (e.g., a lookup/allocation task), do NOT use {task:'job', variable:...} for them -- use the producing task's ref instead (e.g., {task:'<taskId>', variable:'return_data'}), per the merge-task rule: using {task:'job'} for an internally-produced variable incorrectly adds it to inputSchema.required and prompts operators for a value that should never come from them.

Verify the exact 4 required field names against the real resource model file for this use case with: jq '.schema.required' helpers/assets/lcm/<model>.json (or the live model export once pulled) -- do not assume the names match this example verbatim.

merge requires at least 2 items in data_to_merge (satisfied here) and duplicate keys across merged objects produce arrays instead of overwriting -- not a concern in this single flat merge, but worth checking if any of these 4 keys also appear elsewhere upstream.

This merge's merged_object must be wired into whatever task actually performs the LCM instance write (e.g., the runAction/instance-set step, or the workflow's own outputSchema/instance job variable) so all 4 fields land in the written instance.
